topic.title: Turning off the display of text on buttons
topic.para: You can turn off the display of text on buttons. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the Helpers tab of the Options dialog box, clear the Text On Buttons option.

topic.title: Status bar
topic.para: The Status bar at the top of the screen describes commands and displays instructions.

topic.title: What's New
topic.para: You can learn about the new features added to Solid Edge by reading the What's New help topic. On the Help menu click What's New.

topic.title: Context-sensitive Help
topic.para: You can use the context sensitive Help button on the Main toolbar to get on-line Help about items in the application window, including the commands on menus and toolbars.

topic.title: Help for the active command
topic.para: You can press the F1 key to get on-line Help for an active command.

topic.title: Locking element dimensions on the ribbon bar
topic.para: When using drawing tools such as Line and Arc By Center, you can lock a value on the ribbon bar by pressing the ENTER key or the TAB key. You can unlock the value by pressing the BACKSPACE key.

topic.title: Where to learn more
topic.para: You can use the context sensitive Help button on the Main toolbar to get on-line Help about items in the application window, including the commands on menus and toolbars.

topic.title: What's New?
topic.para: You can learn about the new features added to Solid Edge by reading the What's New help topic. On the Help menu click What's New.

topic.title: Getting help with what you are doing now
topic.para: You can press the F1 key to get on-line Help for an active command.

topic.title: Using value fields on the ribbon bar
topic.para: When using drawing tools such as Line and Arc By Center, you can lock a value on the ribbon bar by pressing the ENTER key or the TAB key. You can unlock the value by pressing the BACKSPACE key.

topic.title: Drawing lines tangent to arcs and circles
topic.para: You can draw a line tangent from an arc or circle. For the first point of the line, click the arc or circle.

topic.title: Selecting Elements to Fillet or Chamfers
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can select elements with the Fillet and Chamfer commands three ways:
1) Click one element and then another.
2) Click at the intersection of two elements.
3) Drag across two elements.

topic.title: Trimming 2D elements
topic.para: You can select elements with the Trim command two ways. 1) Click the portion to trim. 2) Drag across multiple portions to trim. The Extend To Next command works that way too.

topic.title: Drawing connected lines and arcs
topic.para: When using the Line/Arc command, you can switch between drawing lines and arcs by clicking the buttons on the ribbon bar, or by pressing "A" or "L" on the keyboard.

topic.title: Drawing several fillets of the same size at once
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can use the Fillet command to draw several fillets of the same size by keying in the radius on the ribbon bar before placing the fillet. Circle By Center works that way, too.

topic.title: Moving fills
topic.para: You can move a fill – a pattern or solid color placed inside a closed boundary using the Fill command – by dragging its handle and dropping it in another area.

topic.title: Controlling view styles
topic.para: You can display a view with various view styles, including shaded and hidden line. From the Main toolbar, click the drop-down arrow for the Format View button, and then choose one of the styles.

topic.title: Faster display
topic.para: The more windows you have open, the more computer memory is used to keep the display of the windows up to date. Close some windows to make the others display faster.

topic.title: Getting the best graphic performance
topic.para: Smooth shaded display combined with an OpenGL accelerated graphics board provides the best graphic display performance.

topic.title: Rendering selected areas
topic.para: In Virtual Studio, you can use the Render Area command to preview the effect of a view style before rendering the entire scene.

topic.title: Displaying smoother arcs
topic.para: You can control the display quality of a view by specifying the minimum number of lines that represent an arc using the View tab on the Options dialog box. Smaller numbers display faster, but are less smooth. Larger numbers are smoother, but display more slowly.

topic.title: Showing and hiding relationship handles
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can hide relationship handles. On the Tools menu, click Relationship Handles.

topic.title: Connecting 2D elements
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, the Connect relationship can attach a keypoint of one element to another element, or it can connect two keypoints together. Elements connected to one another stay connected, even as the overall shape changes.

topic.title: Aligning horizontally or vertically
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can use the Horizontal/Vertical relationship to make lines horizontal or vertical or to align two keypoints horizontally or vertically. Click the Horizontal/Vertical command, then select a single line, ore select two keypoints to align the points vertically or horizontally.

topic.title: Defining equations with variables
topic.para: You can use the Variable Table to define an equation that relates dimensions or other variables. For example, you can relate the length and width of a rectangle.

topic.title: Setting the size of the locate zone
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can change the size of the mouse cursor's locate zone. On the Tools menu click IntelliSketch. On the IntelliSketch dialog box, click the Cursor tab, and then set the locate zone size. You can change the size of the intent zone there too.

topic.title: Disabling part edge locate
topic.para: When drawing a profile on a complex part, if you do not want to locate existing edges, you can use the Part Edge Locate command on the Main toolbar to disable part edge locate.

topic.title: Controlling which relationships are created automatically
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can customize how IntelliSketch works by setting what relationships it recognizes. On the Tools menu, click IntelliSketch. On the IntelliSketch dialog box, click the Relationships tab, and then set the relationships to recognize.

topic.title: Controlling alignment as you draw
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, the cursor shows horizontal and vertical alignment to keypoints of existing elements as you draw, if the Alignment Indicator is on. On the Tools menu click Alignment Indicator.

topic.title: Temporarily suspending automatically created relationships
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can temporarily suspend IntelliSketch's ability to recognize relationships by holding the ALT key. When you release the ALT key IntelliSketch will again recognize relationships.

topic.title: Positioning the grid origin
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can reposition the Grid origin two ways.
1) Click the Reposition Origin button on the Grid toolbar.
2) Press the F12 key on the keyboard.

topic.title: Using shortcuts with Grid
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can use keyboard shortcuts with Grid. Press <ALT> + X to lock and unlock the X value. Press <ALT> + Y to lock and unlock the Y value. Press the F9 key to turn the dynamic display of Grid coordinates off and on.

topic.title: Including edges in a sketch or profile
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can use the Include command to copy part edges or sketch elements for use in a profile or sketch. Set the Link to Layout option on the options dialog to make the include from layout associative.

topic.title: Do you want a separate window for profiles and sketches?
topic.para: When drawing a sketch or a profile for a feature, you can draw in a new 2-D profile window or in the 3-D model window. From the Tools menu click Options, and on the General tab set your preference for entering Profile/Sketch.

topic.title: Locating part edges
topic.para: You can turn on or off the ability to locate part edges when in a sketch or profile. On the Main toolbar, click the Part Edge Locate command.

topic.title: Copying and pasting sketches
topic.para: You can copy sketch or a profile from one feature and paste it into another sketch or the profile of another feature.

topic.title: Using draft documents as sketch libraries
topic.para: You can copy and paste between Draft and Profile/Sketch. This allows you to use a Draft document as a Profile or Sketch library.

topic.title: Using construction elements
topic.para: In Profile/Sketch, construction elements are used to draw the profile but are not used to create the feature. From the Draw toolbar click the Construction command, and then click an element to toggle between construction and profile.

topic.title: Letting Relationship Assistant define relationships and dimensions for you
topic.para: In the Sketch, Profile, and Draft environments, you can use the Relationship Assistant command to apply relationships and dimensions to geometry. In Draft, this is useful for applying relationships imported from AutoCAD (.DWG) or (.DXF).

topic.title: Quickly editing the profile of a feature
topic.para: You can enter directly into the profile of an existing feature. In PathFinder right click on a feature and then click Edit Profile on the shortcut menu.

topic.title: SmartStep lets you edit, too
topic.para: When using a feature's SmartStep ribbon bar, you can edit any of the previously completed steps by clicking on the button for that step. Once the step is active you can make the changes you desire.

topic.title: The Select Tool offers three ways to edit
topic.para: When you select a feature, the Select Tool lets you edit it three different ways: Click Edit Definition to bring up SmartStep for the selected feature and edit the way it is defined. Click Edit Profile to open its profile. Click Dynamic Edit to dynamically edit its dimensions and any unconstrained geometry.

topic.title: Editing failed features
topic.para: If a feature fails to recompute, you can select it in PathFinder and edit it.

topic.title: Use open profiles to make adaptive features
topic.para: You can use an open profile to create an extruded protrusion or cutout. If the profile is on a planar part face, then its ends will be extended to meet the edges of the face. For protrusions, any adjacent faces will be extended to complete the feature.

topic.title: Deselecting objects
topic.para: Deselecting faces and edges You can deselect edges or faces when using commands such as Round Edge or Add Draft. Hold the SHIFT key and click the edge or face to deselect it.

topic.title: Saving hole settings
topic.para: After you have filled in information on the dialog box for a hole, you can use Saved Settings to save this definition with a name and reuse it later. Other commands, such as Web Network, Mounting Boss, Feature Control Frames, and so on, let you do this as well.

topic.title: Finishing features
topic.para: You can finish a feature by clicking the Finish button on the SmartStep ribbon bar, by pressing the ENTER key, or by clicking the right mouse button.

topic.title: Adding and removing features from patterns
topic.para: You can add features to or remove features from a pattern by using the Select step while editing the pattern. This works for Mirror Copy also.

topic.title: Using sketches to define feature profiles
topic.para: You can create the profile for a feature two ways.
1) Draw it in the Profile step of the feature.
2) Select it from a sketch.

topic.title: Creating cross-section profiles of helixes
topic.para: The cross-section profile of a helix can be parallel or perpendicular to the helix axis. During the first step of the Helix command click the Helix Options button and set parallel or perpendicular.

topic.title: Editing the dimensions of many features at once
topic.para: You can display and edit dimensions of multiple features at once. Select all the features at once, and then click the Dynamic Edit button on the Select Tool ribbon bar.

topic.title: Importing Parasolid surfaces
topic.para: You can use the Part Copy command to import a Parasolid surface as a construction surface.

topic.title: Customizing the available hole sizes
topic.para: You can customize the list of hole sizes that appear in the Hole Options dialog box. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the File Locations tab, the Custom Settings file saves custom hole settings.

topic.title: Using Fast and Smart pattern options
topic.para: The Fast pattern option creates simple patterns more quickly when all pattern members interact with the same set of geometry.. The Smart option can intelligently compute feature extents for each member of a pattern.

topic.title: Administering Solid Edge installations consistently
topic.para: Administrators in offices where consistent use of Solid Edge is important can control dozens of options - such as the locations of external files, revision conventions, Insight cache management, link management, and so forth - by running the Solid Edge Administrator.

On the Solid Edge installation CD, copy SptTools\SEAdmin\SEAdmin.exe to the Solid Edge Program folder on the administrator's computer. Run this utility to create configuration files that enforce consistent standards.

topic.title: Working with 3D curves
topic.para: You can create a 3D curves with the Intersection Curve, Project Curve, or Keypoint Curve commands.
Use these curves as sections or paths for sweep and loft features, or use them to create surfaces with the Blue Surf command.

topic.title: Explore the rounding options
topic.para: The Round Edge command has several settings for how the round feature interacts with other geometry in the part. On the Round Edge ribbon bar, click the Round Options button.

topic.title: Adding draft from a parting line
topic.para: You can use the Add Draft command to draft from a parting line. The parting line can be an intersection curve or projected curve.
The Add Draft command has a Split Draft option to create opposing draft angles on either side of a parting line or parting face.

topic.title: Adding draft and parting a model using the same construction surface
topic.para: If you add draft using a construction surface as a parting surface, you can use the same construction surface with the Divide Part command.

topic.title: Adding or removing material with a Lip feature
topic.para: A Lip feature can add or remove material to result in a lip or groove, depending on the direction you specify for the height and width.

topic.title: Creating rounds with varying radius
topic.para: The Variable Radius option in the Round command allows you to enter radius values at points along an edge. Endpoints and midpoints can be selected directly. You can also create intersection points along the edge and enter a radius value for the intersection point.

topic.title: Adding draft to all perpendicular faces at once
topic.para: The Add Draft command has an option to select all faces that are perpendicular to the draft direction.

topic.title: Using construction surfaces for feature extents
topic.para: You can use a construction surface as the extent face for a feature when you use the From/To Extent option.

topic.title: Thinning an entire model or just parts of it
topic.para: The Thin Region command thins a feature or select set of faces, and the Thin-Wall command thins the entire part.

topic.title: Steps for designing cast and molded parts
topic.para: You can build a conceptual model and then divide it into individual parts with the Divide Part command. Then, you can continue adding detail to the individual parts.

topic.title: Changing the units of measurement
topic.para: You can change the units of length, angle, area, volume, mass, and density measurements for each file individually. On the File menu, click File Properties. These values are set on the Units tab and the Advanced Units dialog box.

topic.title: Using the material table
topic.para: You can define behavioral and display characteristics of materials, including the thickness and bend properties of sheet metal parts, using the material table. On the Tools menu, click Material Table.

topic.title: Saving flat patterns
topic.para: You can save a flat pattern of a sheet metal model directly from the 3D part. On the File menu, click Save as Flat.

topic.title: Creating normal cutouts
topic.para: The normal cutout command creates cutouts whose side faces are perpendicular to the faces of the parts they are applied to. In sheet metal, this ensures the cutouts are modeled as they would be punched. In machined parts, this ensures the cutouts are manufacturable.

topic.title: Applying bend and corner relief to flanges
topic.para: Sheet Metal's Flange and Contour Flange features have options for bend relief and corner relief. On the SmartStep ribbon bar, click the Options button.

topic.title: Omit rounding of sheet metal deformation features to improve performance
topic.para: Sheet metal deformation features have an option to exclude rounding to improve recompute and display performance.

topic.title: Creating contour flanges along chains of edges
topic.para: You can create a contour flange along a chain of edges. On the Contour Flange ribbon bar, click the Chain option during the extent step, and then click the edges on which you want to place the flange.

topic.title: Displaying axes of cylindrical and revolved features
topic.para: You can display the center line of any revolved feature or cylindrical face and use it to establish relationships when drawing a profile. On the Tools menu, point to Show All and click Toggle Axes, and then click a feature.

topic.title: Resizing reference planes
topic.para: You can change the size of the reference planes. Select a reference plane, and on the ribbon bar, click Dynamic Edit. Then drag any of the handles on the edges of the plane.

topic.title: Showing and hiding objects
topic.para: You can show and hide anything in the feature or assembly tree of your models. Right-click the object itself or its entry in PathFinder, and select the show or hide command from the shortcut menu.

topic.title: Modifying dimensions by dragging
topic.para: You can modify a dimension by dragging its text, arrow head, or dimension line.

topic.title: Toggling dimensions between driven and driving
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can change a dimension from driving to driven, or from driven to driving. Select a dimension. On the Dimension ribbon bar, click the Driving button.

topic.title: SmartDimension dimensions lines, arcs, circles, and curves
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can change the dimension being placed with the Length, Angle, Radius, and Diameter buttons on the ribbon bar. Click a line, and then click the Angle button to change from Length to Angle.

topic.title: Defining dimension styles
topic.para: The appearance of a dimension is defined by its style. On the Format menu, click Style, choose Dimension as Style Type, and then choose a style from the list to modify or click the New button to create a new style.

topic.title: Dimensioning along horizontal and vertical axes
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can place horizontal and vertical dimensions on a line with SmartDimension, even if the line is at an angle. When placing the dimension, hold the SHIFT key for a horizontal or vertical dimension.

topic.title: Dimensioning tangent to circles and arcs
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can dimension tangent to a circle or arc. On the dimension ribbon bar click the Orientation list, then click By 2 Points.

topic.title: Scrolling dimension values
topic.para: Select a dimension and scroll its value with a wheel mouse.

topic.title: Adding dimensions to stacks, chains, and coordinate groups
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can add dimensions to a stack, chain, or coordinate group. Select the appropriate dimension command and click an existing group for the origin element, and then click a measurement element.

topic.title: Entering multi-line subfixes and prefixes
topic.para: You can enter multiple lines of text in the Subfix field on the Dimension Prefix dialog box. Enter text then press SHIFT+ENTER to begin a new line.

topic.title: Naming and reusing feature control frame settings
topic.para: You can save and reuse the settings of a feature control frame. On the dialog box, enter a name in the Saved Setting box, and then click the Save button. To reuse the settings, click the list on the command ribbon bar and select a name.

topic.title: Inserting vertexes in leaders
topic.para: You can insert a vertex in a leader. Select the leader, and then hold the ALT key and click on the leader line. To remove a vertex, hold the ALT key and click the vertex.

topic.title: Correlating part item number balloons with parts lists
topic.para: You can add item number balloons to parts in a drawing view, and then create a parts list that reflects your item numbers. Or, you can use auto balloon to automatically assign item numbers.

topic.title: Connecting balloon shapes together
topic.para: You can connect balloon shapes together. When placing a balloon, click on an existing balloon to connect to it. You can also drag a balloon and drop it on another to connect to it.

topic.title: Numbering subassemblies in parts lists
topic.para: In a parts list you can exclude individual parts or assemblies. You can also list a subassembly as one item, or list the parts in the subassembly as individual items.

topic.title: Placing driving dimensions
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, when you place a driving dimension on an element, you can edit the value of the dimension to change the element. On the dimension command ribbon bar, toggle the driving/driven option.

topic.title: Mirroring 2D elements
topic.para: In Profile or Sketch, you can use the Mirror command to flip horizontal or vertical, mirror about a line by clicking a line, or mirror about a line by clicking two points.

topic.title: Copying elements using the CTRL key and dragging
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can copy an element by holding the CTRL key and dragging the element.

topic.title: Copying elements while moving, rotating, mirroring, and scaling
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can copy elements when using the Move, Rotate, Mirror, and Scale commands. On the command ribbon bar, click the Copy button, or hold the CTRL key before placing the elements.

topic.title: Choosing how many actions you can undo
topic.para: You can set the number of actions you can undo. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the General tab, and set the number of undo steps. Setting this number high lets you undo more steps, but it consumes more memory, which might make your system less performant.

topic.title: Removing relationships from 2D elements
topic.para: In Sketch or Profile, you can remove relationships when you modify an element. Hold the ALT key and drag the element or one of its handles.

topic.title: Working with multiple selections
topic.para: You can select elements with the Select Tool by dragging a fence or by holding the SHIFT key and clicking elements. You can also deselect elements this way. Clear the select set by pressing the ESC key or by clicking in empty space.

topic.title: Using QuickPick
topic.para: You can use QuickPick to select one of multiple overlapping elements. Pause the Select Tool over the elements. When the ellipsis appears, right-click, and then select one of the elements from the QickPick list.

You can modify QuickPick to use the left or right mouse button, to appear more slowly or quickly, and to display larger or smaller. Invoke QuickPick, then click the options button at the top of the QuickPick list.

topic.title: Selecting from the model or from PathFinder
topic.para: You can select a part or feature with the Select Tool in the graphic window or in PathFinder. Select or deselect more than one by holding the SHIFT key and clicking. Clear the select set by pressing the ESC key or by clicking in empty space.

topic.title: Using shortcut menus
topic.para: Shortcut menus contain commands that are relevant to the selected element. To display a shortcut menu, click the right mouse button when the mouse cursor is over the element.

Shortcut menus also contain commands that are relevant to environment or command context. Right-click away from elements in PathFinder or in the graphic workspace to display commands that are useful there.

topic.title: Filtering what the Select Tool locates
topic.para: You can define the element types that the Select Tool locates. On the Select Tool ribbon bar, click the Select Filter button.

topic.title: Finding parts in large or dense assemblies
topic.para: You can use the Find Part tool to select parts by searching for properties, such as material or keyword. On the Select Tool ribbon bar, click the Find Part button.

topic.title: Hiding parts that clutter assembly views
topic.para: You can use the Select Visible Parts tool in conjunction with the Show Only command to hide parts that are behind visible parts in the view. You can then save a configuration and use it in Draft to improve the performance of creating a drawing view.

topic.title: Saving and applying assembly configurations
topic.para: You can save the current state of all parts in the assembly as a configuration. This includes the shown/hidden, active/inactive, simplified/designed states of all parts. On the Tools menu choose Configuration, and then click Display Configurations, and then name and save a new configuration. You can reapply the configuration later using the Assembly Configurations list on the Select Tool ribbon bar.

topic.title: Making parts in assemblies unselectable
topic.para: You can change a part in an assembly so that it cannot be selected in the graphic window. Select the part. From the Edit menu, click Occurrence Properties, and then set the Selectable option to No. The part can still be selected with PathFinder.

topic.title: Renaming components of assemblies
topic.para: You can rename components of an assembly two ways. Select the part.
1) Select the occurrence, on the Edit menu click Occurrence Properties, and change the Placement Name value.

2) On the Tools menu, click Options, and on the Manage tab, in the Document Name Formula field, click Change and use the Document Name Formula dialog box to define a document name based on file property values.

topic.title: Closing in-place activated parts and subassemblies
topic.para: You can press the ESC key to close an in-place activated part and return to the topmost level of your assembly.

topic.title: Hiding parts in subassemblies
topic.para: You can prevent a part from being displayed in higher level assemblies. Right-click the part, and then click Occurrence Properties. Clear the Display When Assembly Is Attached As Subassembly option.

topic.title: Applying style overrides to parts in assemblies
topic.para: In assemblies you can override the original face styles - colors, textures, and so forth - of parts. From the Tools menu make sure Show and Allow Assembly Style Overrides is checked. Select a part and then select a face style.

topic.title: Displaying exploded views of assemblies
topic.para: You can display an exploded view of your assembly in the Explode environment using the Automatic Explode command. You can use other commands in the Explode environment to make adjustments to the explosion.

topic.title: Showing and hiding reference geometry in assemblies
topic.para: You can show or hide the reference geometry (planes, sketches, coordinate systems, constructions, and axes) in assemblies. While placing a part, on the ribbon bar click Construction Display and select the reference geometry to display. Or, select a part in PathFinder, and on the shortcut menu choose Show/Hide Component and set one of the options.

topic.title: Updating parts and assemblies with inter-part relationships
topic.para: Parts and assemblies with inter-part relationships - such as tubes, wires, and parts with inter-part copies - do not update automatically. To update these relationships, on the Tools menu, choose Update, and click All Links.

topic.title: Saving the result of interference analysis as a part in an assembly
topic.para: You can save the result of interference analysis as a part in the assembly for visualization. On the Check Interference ribbon bar, click Options, and then click Save Interference Volume as Part.

topic.title: Ignoring interference resulting from fasteners and holes with thread attributes
topic.para: You can ignore interference resulting from fasteners and holes with thread attributes. In the Check Interference options dialog, set the Ignore Thread Interferences option.

topic.title: Binding a subassembly and exploding it as a single entity
topic.para: In the Explode environment, you can bind a subassembly and explode it as a single entity. On the Explode toolbar, click Bind Subassembly, and then click a subassembly in PathFinder.

topic.title: Building a select set of parts by querying for properties
topic.para: You can use the Select Tools tab on the EdgeBar tool to build a select set of parts by querying for properties in part files. You can then use the select set as input for any operation that accepts select sets. To perform a query with the select set, double-click on the query name in the Select Tools tab. To add to the existing select set, hold down the CTRL key while you double-click on the query name.

topic.title: Unloading hidden parts to reduce the amount of memory used
topic.para: The Unload Hidden Parts command removes hidden parts from memory, making your computer more responsive. This is a cornerstone of working with large assemblies efficiently.

topic.title: Working with inactive parts
topic.para: When a part is inactive, only the display data of the part is in memory. Inactive parts are visible, but you cannot add or edit relationships without making them active, which loads all of the part information to memory. Loading less information to memory makes a computer more responsive.

topic.title: Making inactive parts active
topic.para: When you open an assembly, all parts are inactive by default. Select the parts you want to work with and then click the Activate command.

topic.title: Opening assemblies with active parts as last saved
topic.para: You can open an assembly with active parts as last saved by turning off the activation override setting on the Open dialog box.

topic.title: Showing only the parts you want to see
topic.para: The Show Only command helps you focus on a subset of parts in a complex assembly. Select the parts that are of interest and then click the Show Only button.

topic.title: Working with parts that are obscured by other parts
topic.para: To work on a part that is visually covered by other parts, try using the Select Visible Parts and Hide commands.

topic.title: Understanding Assembly PathFinder icons
topic.para: The assembly PathFinder displays a unique icon next to each part and assembly to indicate if it is active, inactive, shown, hidden, fully positioned, needs additional relationships, or has conflicting relationships.

topic.title: Placing bolts in holes in one operation
topic.para: You can place a bolt in a hole in one operation. Using FlashFit, click the circular edge of the bolt and then click the circular edge of the hole.

topic.title: Populating holes with fastener stacks
topic.para: You can use the Fastener System command to populate one or more holes with the appropriate fastener stack. This command requires the Solid Edge Standard Parts Library.

topic.title: Capturing assembly relationships in a part for rapid repetitive placement
topic.para: You can capture relationships used to position a part and reuse them later in the same or other assemblies. Either:
1) During Place Part, select the Options dialog and set the Automatically Capture Fit During Place Part option
OR
2) Right-click a part in the assembly and select Capture Fit from the shortcut menu.

topic.title: Setting options that affect how parts are placed
topic.para: Some options for placing parts are only available from the context menu in the Parts Library.
Position the cursor over Parts Libray, ensure that nothing is selected, and right-click to display options used during Place Part.

topic.title: Creating new parts in-place within assemblies
topic.para: You can create a new part in-place within an assembly. Click the Create In-Place button on the Part Library tab of the EdgeBar tool. Select a placement method to define where the part will be placed in the assembly.

topic.title: Maintaining relationships in assemblies
topic.para: When you use assembly relationships to position parts in the assembly, the parts will be placed as grounded parts if the Maintain Relationships check box is cleared on the shortcut menu for the Part Library tab of the EdgeBar tool.

topic.title: Using the Zoom and Pan command
topic.para: When using the Zoom or Pan command, you can click the mouse or drag for dynamics.

topic.title: Keyboard shortcuts to view commands
topic.para: You can set a view to the default isometric orientation by pressing CTRL+I. Try CTRL+F, CTRL+T, CTRL+R, CTRL+L, and CTRL+B also.

topic.title: Rotating views of parts and assemblies with the mouse
topic.para: To rotate the view of a part or assembly, hold the scroll wheel down and move the mouse.

topic.title: Improving the performance of creating drawing views
topic.para: With the Show Only command, use the Select Visible Parts option to hide parts that are behind visible parts in the view. You can then save a configuration and use it in Draft to improve the performance of creating a drawing view.

topic.title: Fitting the whole drawing sheet
topic.para: You can fit the whole drawing sheet. Hold the SHIFT key and click the Fit command.

topic.title: Customizing how Zoom Tool works
topic.para: You can customize how Zoom Tool works. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the View tab.

topic.title: Keyboard shortcut to activate Zoom Tool
topic.para: You can activate Zoom Tool directly from the keyboard by holding the ALT and Z keys. The Zoom tool will terminate when you press the ESC key.

topic.title: Using viewing commands without interrupting the active command
topic.para: You can use viewing commands without interrupting the active command. Hold the SHIFT key and drag with the right mouse button to rotate. Hold CTRL and drag to zoom, or hold both CTRL and SHIFT to pan. Hold ALT and drag to zoom area, or ALT click to fit.

topic.title: Emailing Solid Edge files
topic.para: You can email Solid Edge files. On the File menu, choose Send To and click Mail Recipient.

topic.title: Editing the properties of all files in a folder or assembly
topic.para: You can edit the properties of all files in a folder or assembly using the Property Manager command. On the Tools menu, click Property Manager.

topic.title: Getting assistance setting up Insight Server
topic.para: Need help setting up Insight? You can get automated assistance validating and configuring the underlying components Insight relies upon, installing Insight Server, and building new document libraries. In the Solid Edge Program folder, run the file, Insight Server Assistant.exe.

topic.title: Displaying the status of managed documents
topic.para: Using Insight, you can show who has a file checked out and if there is a new revision or new version of a file. In EdgeBar, on the shortcut menu, click Display Status.

topic.title: Controlling how files are named in Assembly PathFinder
topic.para: In Assembly, you can control how files are named in PathFinder by creating a formula. On the Tools menu, click Options. Then, on the Options dialog box, display the Manage tab. Change the document name formula to construct a name using document properties such as document title, part number, project name, and so forth.

topic.title: Creating new revisions of parts in assemblies
topic.para: If you are using Insight, you can create a new revision of a part in an assembly from the PathFinder shortcut menu. Right-click the document in Assembly PathFinder and click Revisions.

topic.title: Applying a cutaway views to assemblies
topic.para: You can apply a cutaway view to see internal components of an assembly. Keep in mind that some time is taken to recompute a cutaway if parts are added, deleted, changed, moved, shown, or hidden.

topic.title: Using templates
topic.para: A template is a document that gets copied to create a new document. A template is like any other document. You can open it, work in it, and save it. If you often perform the same steps to begin a task, you can perform those steps and then save the document as a template.

topic.title: Opening recently used files
topic.para: The File menu contains a list of recently opened files. Click one to open it. You can define the number of files in the list. On the Tools menu click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the General tab, and set the number of entries.

topic.title: Prevent others from editing documents that are in work
topic.para: You can prevent others from editing a document by changing its status to In Work. On the File menu, click Properties, click the Status tab, and then change the status to In Work. Others can open and read the document, but they cannot save changes.

topic.title: Copy assemblies and all their linked parts
topic.para: You can use Revision Manager to copy an assembly and all its linked parts. The links in the assembly are updated to reference the new parts. See on-line Help for details of Revision Manager.

topic.title: Controlling the display of drawing views when they are created
topic.para: The settings on the Edge Display tab on the Options dialog box control the display of a drawing view when it is created. You can change the display of an existing drawing view with the Properties command on drawing view ribbon.

topic.title: Controlling the display of each part in a drawing view of an assembly
topic.para: You can control the display of each part in an assembly when using the View Of Part command. On the View Of Part ribbon bar, click Model Display Settings, click a part in the list, and then set the show or hide selected part option.

topic.title: Controlling which parts of an assembly are sectioned in a drawing view
topic.para: You can control which parts of an assembly are sectioned when using the Section View command. On the Section View ribbon click Model Display Settings, click a part in the list and then set or clear the Section Selected Part option.

topic.title: Changing the drawing sheet that a drawing view is placed on
topic.para: You can change the drawing sheet that a drawing view is placed on. Select the drawing view. On the drawing view ribbon click Properties, click the General tab and then change the sheet.

topic.title: Changing the scale of a drawing view
topic.para: You can change the scale of a drawing view. Select the drawing view. On the Drawing View ribbon click Properties, click the General tab and then change the scale.

topic.title: Drawing new geometry in a drawing view created from a part or assembly
topic.para: You can draw in a drawing view created from a part or assembly. Right-click the drawing view and then click the Draw in View command on the shortcut menu. Click Return on the ribbon to close the drawing view.

topic.title: Applying assembly configurations when placing drawing views
topic.para: You can select an assembly configuration when placing a drawing view. If you select an explode configuration, you can place an exploded assembly view.

topic.title: Reducing the size of Draft files
topic.para: You can reduce the size of a Draft file by deleting elements that are not displayed. On the Tools menu click the Reduce File command.

topic.title: Creating views of complex assemblies very quickly
topic.para: You can quickly create views of complex assemblies. Create Draft Quality views first, dimension and annotate your drawings, and then convert the views to High Quality before you print.

topic.title: Copying prefix and tolerance information
topic.para: Prefix Copier copies prefix information or tolerances or both. On the Prefix Copier ribbon click the Copy What box and then select what you want to copy.

topic.title: Editing predefined colors for highlight, select, background, and more
topic.para: Solid Edge has predefined colors for highlight, select, background, and more. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the Colors tab. You can set these colors to any value that works best for you.

topic.title: Viewing the parents and children of a feature
topic.para: You can quickly see the parents and children of a feature. Right-click the feature and select Show Parents and Children.

topic.title: Specifying where Solid Edge looks for templates and other files
topic.para: You can specify where Solid Edge looks for templates and other files. On the Tools menu click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the File Location tab.

topic.title: Adding and removing toolbar buttons
topic.para: You can move a button to a different toolbar by holding the ALT key, dragging the button, and dropping it on another toolbar. You can remove the button by dropping it in a window. You can add new buttons to toolbars. On the Tools menu, click Customize. Drag buttons from the Toolbars tab to the toolbar you want to add them to.

topic.title: Hiding scroll bars, sheet tabs, and other items
topic.para: In the Draft environment, you can hide scroll bars, sheet tabs, and other items. On the Tools menu click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the View tab.

topic.title: Creating custom colors while drawing
topic.para: While drawing 2D elements, you can create custom colors. On the ribbon bar, click the Color select list, click More, and then create a color on the custom color palette.

topic.title: Hiding the unit label that appears in value boxes
topic.para: You can hide the unit label that appears in value boxes. On the Tools menu, click Options. On the Options dialog box, click the General tab, and then clear the Display Unit of Measurement Label check box.

topic.title: Creating custom keyboard shortcuts
topic.para: You can create custom keyboard shortcuts to help you perform your tasks more efficiently. On the Tools menu, click Customize. Click on the Keyboard tab and make the keyboard assignments.

topic.title: Docking and un-docking EdgeBar
topic.para: Double-clicking in the title-bar of EdgeBar when it is un-docked will return it to the last docked location. You can keep EdgeBar from docking by holding the CTRL key while dragging it.

topic.title: Reordering features, reference planes, and sketches of a part
topic.para: You can reorder features, reference planes, and sketches of a part. From PathFinder drag features up the tree to reorder.

topic.title: Replaying the feature sequence of parts
topic.para: You can replay the feature sequence of a part. On the Feature Playback tab in EdgeBar, use the arrow controls to review your part.

topic.title: Inserting features in the state trees of parts
topic.para: You can insert a feature in the state tree of a part. Right click a feature in PathFinder and select GoTo, and then place features. When done inserting use GoTo again on the last feature in PathFinder.

topic.title: Creating flight paths
topic.para: You can use the Flight Plan Wizard to populate the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar with a flight path. Once the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar is populated, commands can be accessed on the timeline to modify the flight path. On the Animate toolbar, click the Flight Plan Wizard button.

topic.title: Deleting key frames from flight paths
topic.para: You can delete a key frame from a flight path by clicking on a Key Frame Indicator and dragging it off of the timeline.

topic.title: Displaying flight paths
topic.para: You can graphically display the flight path in the graphic window . On the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar, click the Show Flight Path button.

topic.title: Undocking the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar
topic.para: You can undock the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar by clicking on the background and dragging it out of the area in which it is currently docked.

topic.title: Accessing commands to edit flight paths
topic.para: You can access commands that will help you edit the flight path by right-clicking the mouse over the background of the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar.

topic.title: Saving flight paths in .AVI format
topic.para: You can save your flight path as an .AVI. On the File menu, click Save as Movie.

topic.title: Adding frames and time to flight paths
topic.para: You can add frames or time to your flight path. Right click on the background of the Timeline and Playback ribbon bar, then click the Add Frames button or Add Time button. You can also remove frames or time.

topic.title: Adding soft shadows to models with Virtual Studio+
topic.para: With Virtual Studio+ you can add soft shadows to your model from point, spot, directional and other light sources.

topic.title: Creating artistic renderings with Virtual Studio+
topic.para: With Virtual Studio+, you can create artistic style renditions of your model to create a hand-drawn sketch look.

topic.title: Creating scenes with Virtual Studio+
topic.para: When preparing your models to be rendered, don’t model a base surface; add a scene from within Virtual Studio+

topic.title: Locking to axes and planes when drawing in XpresRoute
topic.para: You can lock to axes and planes when drawing lines in XpresRoute. Click an axis or plane of OrientXpres, or press z to lock an axis or x to lock a plane.

topic.title: Showing and hiding paths of tubes in XpresRoute
topic.para: You can show or hide the path of a tube in XpresRoute. Right click a tube and click Show Path or Hide Path on the shortcut menu.

topic.title: Opening foreign files in Solid Edge
topic.para: You can open an AutoCAD (.DWG) or (.DXF) file as a Solid Edge Draft document. On the Main toolbar click the Open button. On the Open dialog box, choose a file type from the Files Of Type list, then select a file to open. On the New dialog box, select a Draft (.DFT) template, and then click OK.

topic.title: Inspecting imported models
topic.para: You can inspect imported foreign models, display geometry that may contain errors, and gather information to help you understand and resolve the errors. On the Inspect menu, click Geometry Inspector.

topic.title: Save Solid Edge files to other formats
topic.para: You can save your Solid Edge file to a variety of formats. On the File menu, click the Save As command, and then select a format from the Save File As Type list.

topic.title: Implementing standard drawing formats
topic.para: You can implement a standard drawing format using styles. You can modify existing styles or create new styles for lines, dimensions, and text. On the Format menu, select Style.

topic.title: Defining the color, font size, and other properties of dimensions
topic.para: You can define the color, font size, and other properties of dimensions. On the Format menu, select Style. You can create a new dimension style or modify one that exists.

topic.title: Changing the styles of elements
topic.para: You can change the style of an element. Select the element and choose a style from the style list on the ribbon bar.
